title: db-test: migration-count assertions stale (expect 41, actual 43)
description:
## Problem

`cargo test -p sutra --test db-test` has two failing tests on a clean `main` tree:

- `test_fresh_db_creates_schema_migrations` (tests/db-test.rs:786)
- `test_migration_reopen_is_idempotent` (tests/db-test.rs:799)

Both assert `count == 41` against `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations`, but a fresh DB now registers **43** migrations. The assertion message is even staler — it still says "all 37 existing migrations". Migrations were added (e.g. recent lessons/graph work) without bumping these hard-coded counts.

```
assertion `left == right` failed: fresh DB should register all 37 existing migrations
  left: 43
 right: 41
```

## Root cause

The expected migration count is a magic literal duplicated across two tests (and a wrong message string). Every migration addition requires manually updating them, and they drift.

## Fix

Minimum: update both literals to 43 and correct the message. Better (prevents recurrence): derive the expected count from the migration registry/list the code applies (single source of truth) instead of hard-coding, so the test asserts "DB count == number of defined migrations" and never goes stale again.

## Acceptance

- `cargo test -p sutra --test db-test` fully green
- Expected count no longer a bare magic number duplicated across tests (or, if kept literal, message text matches)

## Notes

Found incidentally while fixing sutra/216 (sutra_remember anchors). Unrelated to that change — pre-existing on clean tree. Clippy `never_loop` deny error at src/parser/python.rs:314 is covered by the existing clippy-warnings task, not this one.
root_cause: Migration count assertions in db-test.rs hardcoded 41 (with a message still saying 37). Migrations were added for lessons/graph work without bumping these literals, so the actual count (43) diverged.
